# Collapsed graph fibers: an exact depth obstruction to deleting an integer coordinate

For every integer s>=1 we construct a full-dimensional convex body C_s in R^3_p x R_u x R^s_x, equal to the convex hull of its actual fine mixed set, with the following properties:

- every coarse integer fiber over p in Z^3 lies in a single hyperplane u=g(p), so its full (s+1)-dimensional volume is zero;
- the original fine lattice is Z^3 x Z in the (p,u) coordinates;
- its fine mixed measure has nine equal positive s-simplex fibers and one zero-mass point fiber;
- its exact maximal normalized fine depth is Gamma_s/9, where Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s.

For s>=2 this depth is strictly BELOW Gamma_(s+1)/8. Therefore no rule that simply deletes the fine integer-coordinate constraint, retains the original fine depth, and uses the coarse rank-three target Gamma_(s+1)/8 can be valid in this zero-coarse-volume setting. This is not an OC counterexample: the actual fine integer rank is four, whose target is Gamma_s/16.

## 1. The body and its exact integer fibers

Use P,g,W and the indices of `candidate 5c9190df7c42c598`. In particular

    W={0,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10},
    g_2=1/2,

and every other g_i is an integer. The only additional integral graph point is i=9. The function g is Jensen-affine on the lattice-convex eleven-point P.

Let K be the standard s-simplex in R^s, with volume V>0, and fix k_0=0 in K. Define

    C_s = conv( union_(i in W) ({(p_i,g_i)} x K)
                union { (p_9,g_9,k_0) } ).                (1)

This body is full-dimensional in R^(4+s). Indeed the graph points over W have affine span R^4, as proved in the arithmetic note; one positive full s-dimensional fiber then makes the affine hull of (1) all of R^(4+s). Compactness and convexity are immediate.

Its coarse base projection is conv(P). Over ANY integer coarse point p in P, Jensen affinity forces the u-coordinate of every point of C_s to be exactly g(p). Thus all coarse (s+1)-volumes are zero, including at the original positive fine fibers.

At a fine integer base the fibers are EXACTLY

    (p_i,g_i): K,        i in W,
    (p_9,g_9): {k_0},

and there are no other fine integer bases. To check this:

1. Projection and Jensen affinity show that a fine integer base must lie in the integral graph T, which consists of these ten points.
2. At each W point, the fiber contains its given K and is contained in K because every continuous x-coordinate used in (1) belongs to K.
3. The point p_9 is exposed away from conv(W) by y+z: its value is 3 there and at most 2 on W. Thus its fiber is exactly the generating point k_0.

The actual fine mixed set S_s=C_s intersect (Z^4 x R^s) has Hausdorff dimension s. Its intrinsic measure mu is the sum of ordinary s-volume over the nine positive fibers; the point fiber has zero mass because s>=1. Therefore

    mu(S_s)=9V.                                         (2)

All generating fibers in (1) lie in S_s, so C_s=conv(S_s) exactly.

The extra coarse point p_2 is not absent geometrically. Its u-coordinate is 1/2, and its x-fiber is exactly K: either midpoint pair (0,6) or (1,3) combines two copies of K to K. Hence removing the fine integrality condition actually adds a full positive intrinsic fiber. It changes the sampled measure and cannot be treated as a harmless relabeling.

## 2. Exact maximal fine depth

At the centroid of K in any W fiber, every containing closed ambient halfspace restricts to an own-fiber halfspace containing that centroid, or to the whole fiber. Ordinary continuous simplex Grunbaum gives own-fiber captured volume at least Gamma_s V. This standard continuous fact is also covered by the fully proved signed-exponential simplex-cap comparison in `candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`. Therefore

    max depth_mu >= Gamma_s/9.                           (3)

For a completely finite matching upper certificate, let lambda_0,...,lambda_s be K's barycentric coordinates. Each of its s+1 caps

    lambda_r(x)>=1/(s+1)

has volume Gamma_s V, and these caps cover K because the coordinates sum to one.

For each i in W take the exposing base normal n_i from the table in the arithmetic note. Its value at p_i exceeds its value at every other W base by at least one. Thus the following actual ambient closed caps isolate these simplex caps among all positive fine fibers:

    lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)
       +2 n_i dot (p-p_i) >=0,       0<=r<=s.            (4)

At its own base this is the desired simplex cap. At any other positive base, lambda_r(x)<=1 and n_i dot(p-p_i)<=-1, so the margin is strictly negative. The point fiber at p_9 may be included but contributes zero mass. Consequently every cap (4) has exactly Gamma_s V mass.

The 9(s+1) caps in (4) cover all positive fibers. Add the one cap

    y+z>=3,                                              (5)

which contains p_9 and excludes every positive fine base. Its mass is zero. These finitely many closed caps cover the entire actual fine mixed set, including the zero-mass point. Therefore every mixed point has depth at most Gamma_s/9. At p_9 its depth is zero by (5). Combined with (3),

    max_(a in S_s) depth_mu(a) = Gamma_s/9.               (6)

No product-depth or tensorization principle is used here: both the own-fiber lower bound and every cap in the finite upper cover are explicit.

## 3. The strict dimension-sensitive comparison

For real t>0 set F(t)=t log(t/(t+1))=log Gamma_t. Direct differentiation gives

    F''(t)=1/[t(t+1)^2]>0.

Thus F(t+1)-F(t) is strictly increasing, and consequently

    Gamma_(s+1)/Gamma_s >= Gamma_2/Gamma_1 = 8/9,

with equality only when s=1. Therefore

    Gamma_s/9 = Gamma_(s+1)/8    when s=1,
    Gamma_s/9 < Gamma_(s+1)/8    for every s>=2.          (7)

For example s=2 gives 4/81 < 27/512.

The true fine OC target Gamma_s/16 is strictly smaller than (6), so this construction does not violate that target. Nor does it contradict applying OC to the DIFFERENT coarse mixed source: that source includes the fractional-height p_2 fiber and is not the original fine measure. The proved obstruction is specifically to transferring the coarse rank-three bound back to the original fine source by deleting the integrality condition without further mass or incidence control.

## 4. Exact checks

The arithmetic note's verifier checks every base, height, exposure gap, and full graph rank used in (1)--(5). The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_collapsed_graph_simplex_depth.py` checks the cap-isolation algebra, exact s=1 equality and rational s>=2 comparisons over a finite range, and independently verifies the all-real derivative identity in Section 3. The calculus proof, rather than the finite checks, establishes (7) for all s.

This is an exact lower-coarse-dimensional example with the full fine hull retained. It isolates a real arithmetic obstruction to naive rank deletion; it does not solve the remaining multi-component mass allocation problem.
